title: Cornel iridoid glycosides exerted neuroprotective effects against cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury in rats via inhibiting TLR4/MyD88/NF-kappaB pathway.
authors: Guo, Rui; Xue, Fangli; Zhang, Jianmei; Li, Jing; Li, Huiliang; Qiao, Boling
one_liner_zh: 该文研究山茱萸环烯醚萜苷通过抑制TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB通路发挥脑缺血再灌注损伤的神经保护作用，分子对接仅涉及蛋白-小分子，与蛋白质-DNA互作及TF-DNA结合建模完全无关。
abstract: Inflammatory response plays a key role in the pathophysiological process of Ischemic stroke. Cornel iridoid glycosides (CIG), the primary components of Cornus officinalis Sieb. et Zucc., have demonstrated a wide range of anti-inflammatory pharmacological activities. This study aimed to investigate the neuroprotective effect of CIG against cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury and to explore its anti-inflammatory mechanisms. Sprague-Dawley rats were pre-treated with CIG at doses of 1.25, 2.5, and 5 mL/kg and then subjected to transient middle cerebral artery occlusion/re-perfusion (tMCAO/R). The effectiveness of prevention was determined based on neurological function, cerebral infarction, edema, histological changes, microglia aggregation, and induction of inflammation cytokines using hematoxylin-eosin staining, TUNEL staining, and real-time quantitative PCR. Proteins involved in the canonical nuclear factor kappa B (NF-kappaB) signaling pathway were analyzed using immunofluorescence, western blot, and molecular docking analysis. The results showed that CIG could dose-dependently reduce the neurological deficit score, cerebral infarction and edema, and brain cells apoptosis caused by tMCAO/R injury. Additionally, CIG significantly inhibited the aggregation of microglia and decreased levels of tumor necrosis factor-alpha, interleukin-1beta and interleukin-6 in a dose-dependent manner. Furthermore, the tMCAO/R rats pre-treated with CIG displayed inhibition of NF-kappaB nuclear translocation and down-regulations on TLR4, MyD88, TRAF6, and inhibitory kappa B. Molecular docking analysis revealed that the CIG components (morroniside, loganin, and cornuside I) exhibited good affinities with protein TLR4, MyD88, and TRAF6. CIG could alleviate cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury by inhibiting microglia aggregation and reducing the neuroinflammatory response, which targets the TLR4/MyD88/NF-kappaB signaling pathway. Therefore, CIG might potentially serve as a new medicine candidate for the prevention of ischemic stroke.
abstract_zh: 炎症反应在缺血性脑卒中的病理生理过程中发挥关键作用。山茱萸环烯醚萜苷（CIG）是山茱萸（Cornus officinalis Sieb. et Zucc.）的主要成分，已显示出广泛的抗炎药理活性。本研究旨在探讨CIG对脑缺血/再灌注损伤的神经保护作用，并探索其抗炎机制。Sprague-Dawley大鼠以1.25、2.5和5 mL/kg剂量预给药CIG，随后进行短暂大脑中动脉闭塞/再灌注（tMCAO/R）。通过神经功能、脑梗死、水肿、组织学变化、小胶质细胞聚集及炎症细胞因子诱导情况，采用苏木精-伊红染色、TUNEL染色和实时定量PCR评估预防效果。使用免疫荧光、蛋白质印迹和分子对接分析检测经典核因子κB（NF-kappaB）信号通路相关蛋白。结果显示，CIG可剂量依赖性地降低tMCAO/R损伤引起的神经功能缺损评分、脑梗死和水肿及脑细胞凋亡。此外，CIG显著抑制小胶质细胞聚集，并剂量依赖性地降低肿瘤坏死因子-α、白细胞介素-1β和白细胞介素-6水平。进一步地，预给药CIG的tMCAO/R大鼠表现出NF-kappaB核转位抑制，以及TLR4、MyD88、TRAF6和抑制性κB的下调。分子对接分析显示，CIG成分（莫诺苷、马钱苷和山茱萸苷I）与蛋白TLR4、MyD88和TRAF6具有良好的亲和力。CIG可通过抑制小胶质细胞聚集和减少神经炎症反应来减轻脑缺血/再灌注损伤，其靶向TLR4/MyD88/NF-kappaB信号通路。因此，CIG可能作为预防缺血性脑卒中的新型候选药物。
